entries.title: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure and charters out tankers into October, sources say
entries.claimSummary: QatarEnergy extended force majeure for LNG supplies to several Asian buyers into mid-September.
extractedFacts: Force-majeure notices due to expire in August and early September were extended until mid-September.
Affected buyers include customers in South Korea, India and Bangladesh.
QatarEnergy continued leasing some LNG tankers through mid-October.
At least nine QELM/QET-controlled LNG carriers were sub-chartered to named third parties.
entries.carryReason: Reviewed Sep 11; the Reuters July 23 notice remains a valid historical disclosure, but no newer source-approved replacement is available in this evidence record. Keep the later extension as carried manual context.

entries.title: QatarEnergy seeks US LNG deals through to 2031, sources say
entries.claimSummary: Re-scraped the exact Reuters Sep 11 article. It remains the latest source-approved update reviewed; force-majeure renewals were reported through November and US LNG discussions through 2031.
extractedFacts: Reuters reported QatarEnergy was negotiating multi-year US LNG contracts through 2031 to replace damaged capacity.
The report said two of Ras Laffan's 14 LNG trains and a gas-to-liquids facility were damaged.
The report said QatarEnergy was seeking 2-3 MTPA of US LNG and that force-majeure notices were renewed through November.
entries.carryReason: Reviewed Sep 28: Reuters' Sep 11 report remains the latest source-approved QatarEnergy force-majeure and replacement-supply update, covering renewals through November and 2-3 MTPA of US LNG discussions through 2031. No newer approved update was found.

entries.title: US, Iran engaged in tanker war: Where is the months-long conflict headed?
entries.claimSummary: Al Jazeera reported the US and Iran fought a direct tanker war Sep 5-6: CENTCOM struck three Iranian oil tankers while Iran fired missiles at a US carrier and destroyer and hit three tankers plus three US-linked vessels.
extractedFacts: CENTCOM struck three Iranian oil tankers near Kharg Island, near Jask, and an unladen vessel in the Gulf of Oman after crew evacuation, with no US personnel injured.
Iran launched ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and destroyer, both of which evaded the missiles.
Iran targeted three oil tankers in the Strait and three US-linked vessels elsewhere, and separately claimed to have struck an unmanned US vessel.
CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper warned of an even higher economic cost for further attacks, while Iran's IRGC warned vessels not to transit unauthorised waterways.
entries.carryReason: Reviewed Sep 21; current AP and Reuters reporting still provides no verified signed commercial reopening or verified Hormuz clearance. Al Jazeera's Sep 6 report remains the latest approved direct security evidence of the tanker war in this record.

entries.title: Oil settles up around 4% as Iran's president vows to never surrender
entries.claimSummary: Reuters reported Sep 23 that Saudi Arabia restarted its East-West pipeline to the Red Sea, while indirect US-Iran talks discussed reopening Hormuz and lifting the US naval blockade. Iran's position on reopening remained conditional.
extractedFacts: Brent crude futures settled at 103.08 USD/bbl on Sep 23, up 3.86%; WTI futures settled at 92.16 USD/bbl, up 1.81%.
Saudi Arabia restarted East-West pipeline operations to the Red Sea on Sep 22 after a Sep 11 drone attack halted crude loadings at Yanbu.
Saudi Arabia offered Asian refiners additional barrels from locations outside the Strait of Hormuz.
Indirect talks on Sep 22 discussed reopening the Strait of Hormuz and lifting the US naval blockade on Iranian ports.
A senior Iranian official said Hormuz could reopen within seven days if the United States eased military pressure and lifted its blockade.
Iran's security chief said the Strait would not reopen until Iran's conditions were met.

entries.title: US-Iran conflict helps drive wave of supertanker orders
entries.claimSummary: Reuters reported Sep 17 that Strait of Hormuz tanker crossings remain in single digits (LSEG data) as shipowners order a record wave of VLCCs to serve longer Atlantic-to-Asia routes.
entries.carryReason: Reviewed Sep 21; Reuters' Sep 17 LSEG single-digit tanker-crossing observation remains the latest approved vessel-scope datapoint. The newer Reuters report confirms Saudi oil flows are recovering but does not replace the single-digit crossing count.
extractedFacts: Shipowners ordered 217 Very Large Crude Carriers in 2026 so far, versus 93 in all of 2025, a buying spree worth over $20 billion, per Signal Group data.
Allied Shipbroking recorded 164 VLCC orders in 2026, up from 83 in 2025.

An LSEG chart of Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic (vessels above 10,000 deadweight tonnes) showed crossings remaining in single digits, with the article headline noting crossings remain in single digits.
VLCC spot prices have climbed above $500,000 per day, up from about $132,000 in February before the war, per Allied Shipbroking.
Gulf producers are increasingly shuttling oil out of the Gulf through Hormuz to reload onto larger tankers waiting in the Gulf of Oman, tying up vessels and adding to VLCC demand.

extractedFacts: Kpler data showed 33.7 million barrels of crude oil exited Hormuz during the week beginning Sep 20 as of Sep 25.
Kpler counted nine commodity vessels transiting on Sep 24, down from 14 on Sep 23.
The nine-vessel count was below an 18-vessel 10-day average.
The export tally comprised 19 tankers, including 17 VLCCs.

observations.instrument: Kpler Strait of Hormuz commodity-vessel transit count

entries.carryReason: Reviewed Sep 28: Reuters/Kpler's latest exact daily count is nine commodity vessels on Sep 24, with 33.7 million barrels of crude exports week-to-date reported Sep 25. No Sep 28 daily count was found; carry the dated Sep 24 count.

entries.title: Oil slides as US-Iran truce hopes outweigh Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
entries.claimSummary: Reuters reported Brent settled at 104.32 USD/bbl on Sep 25, down 2.1%, as truce hopes outweighed attack risk. The article also reported Brent at 105.11 at 05:41 GMT, six Houthi missiles intercepted near Taif/Yanbu, and no resumption of Yanbu tanker loadings.
extractedFacts: Brent futures settled at 104.32 USD/bbl on September 25, down 2.28 USD or 2.1 percent.
At 05:41 GMT on September 25, Brent was 105.11 USD/bbl and WTI was 92.61 USD/bbl.
US and Iranian negotiators were exploring a phased path that would involve reopening Hormuz and Washington lifting its economic blockade of Iran.
Saudi Arabia said it intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Houthis toward Taif and the Yanbu area.
East-West pipeline pumping volumes were building, but crude tanker loadings at Yanbu had yet to resume.

entries.title: Gulf of Oman ship-to-ship oil transfers reach limit as Saudi exports surge
entries.claimSummary: Reuters reported September Saudi crude exports via Hormuz on track for 3.6 million bpd, while Gulf of Oman ship-to-ship operations reached capacity. A $1.27 million/day Middle East-to-China VLCC time-charter quote was reported for Sep 21.
extractedFacts: Kpler data put Saudi crude exports through Hormuz on track for 3.6 million bpd in September, up from about 0.9 million bpd in August.
Gulf of Oman ship-to-ship transfers for Middle East oil reached their limits, with queues for tugboats and labour.
Reuters reported a $1.27 million/day Middle East-to-China VLCC time-charter rate on Monday, September 21.
The charter rate is not a route-normalised per-barrel freight assessment and does not replace the carried $11.50/bbl quote.

entries.title: Strait of Hormuz tensions linger as Iran and US move further from a deal
entries.claimSummary: Al Jazeera reported Sep 27 that Tehran instructed shipping companies to use a temporary Iran-approved Hormuz route and pay fees; full reopening remains conditional on ending the US blockade. Reports of explosions were attributed to Iranian media and were not confirmed by Iranian authorities.
extractedFacts: Al Jazeera reported Tehran instructed shipping companies transiting Hormuz to use a temporary route approved by Iranian authorities and pay relevant fees.
Iran said the strait would not fully reopen until the US blockade on Iranian ports ends.
Iranian media reported explosions near Qeshm Island; the article said Iranian authorities had not confirmed attacks that day.
Trump rejected Iran's seven-day proposal; Iran's foreign minister said Tehran would await an official response through mediators.

entries.title: Mideast oil exports rebound in September as Saudi Arabia boosts shipments
entries.claimSummary: Reuters/Kpler reported Sep 28 that Middle East crude exports rebounded in September, Hormuz exports were set for about 7.4 million bpd, and Saudi/Ras Tanura exports recovered while remaining below February.
extractedFacts: Kpler put key Middle East crude exports at 12.8 million bpd in September, still about 6 million bpd below February's 18.8 million bpd.
Hormuz exports were set to reach about 7.4 million bpd in September.
Saudi crude exports were on track for about 5.4 million bpd in September, compared with 2.446 million bpd in August.
Ras Tanura shipments were about 3.6 million bpd versus 929,000 bpd in August and 6.411 million bpd in February.
Kpler counted 19 very large crude carriers carrying Saudi oil exiting Hormuz the prior week; vessels with transponders off are excluded.
